subject: Unexpected windowed usage spike / request for billing breakdown
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@storify.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@storify.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Charge spike on Nov 30 invoice — request for evidence

Hi Ben,

We just received invoice INV-STOR-202711 and there is a large >2.5x jump in usage on Nov 30 compared to our 30‑day baseline. AP flagged a $12,300 line item for "Windowed usage (Nov 30 02:00–05:00 UTC)" and wants an explanation before we release payment.

Can you send a breakdown of the calls that contributed to that window (endpoints, model variants, per-request token counts) and any indicators of replayed/batched traffic? We attach our internal sampling showing repeated session IDs.

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform, Storify.ai
olivia@storify.ai

Attachments: storify_sample_ids.txt (50 lines)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@storify.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Charge spike on Nov 30 invoice — request for evidence

Hi Olivia — thanks for the heads up and for sending the sample IDs.

We pulled the meter and see the same concentrated window between 02:05–04:52 UTC on Nov 30. Preliminary notes:
- Traffic hit our inference cluster in US‑west with sustained concurrent sessions that caused multiple burst-scaled allocations (autoscaling policy 3).
- A single client IP group accounted for ~62% of the windowed tokens; request headers suggest repeated short conversations rather than long single sequences (many calls with ~320–800 tokens each).
- We see at least 3 reconnects from the same session ids which may have caused duplicate prefix caching misses.

I'm copying Priyom from our billing/telemetry team to grab raw logs and a token-level CSV. Priyom — can you generate a per-request export (timestamp, request_id, model_variant, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, user_agent) for 2027-11-30 01:30–06:00 UTC?

Olivia — we want to get this cleared for your AP team quickly. If anything looks like a replay/ingest duplication on our side we'll propose a retro credit. If it's legitimate production traffic we can offer a one‑time courtesy smoothing credit to help with your close.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Sales, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachments: —

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@storify.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 10:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Charge spike on Nov 30 invoice — request for evidence

Hi all — exported the requested slice and attached a condensed CSV (2027-11-30_storify_usage_snapshot.csv). Quick summary from telemetry:

- Total window tokens (02:00–05:00 UTC): 1,125,420 tokens.
- Top model variant: redwood-xl-8q (75% of tokens).
- 1,834 requests from the same client IP block (203.0.113.0/24).
- 412 request_ids show identical prompt hashes across reconnects (likely retry or client-side replay).
- Average completion token per affected request: 475.

Notes and suggestions:
- The root cause appears to be client-side retries producing duplicate requests during a period of transient network instability — we see fast reconnects with same conversation_id and identical prompts. That pattern results in billing for separate inference calls (we bill per completed token).
- We do not see evidence of server-side duplication or double-billing on our ingestion layer.

Proposal: because at least ~28% of the windowed tokens come from suspected client replays, we recommend a targeted adjustment: 28% credit on the windowed line item ($3,444) and a separate technical note for Storify to adjust their client retry logic (idempotency tokens / backoff).

If you want a more conservative credit, we can run a deeper correlation and provide hashed-prompt-level de‑duplication evidence (will take ~2 business days).

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Billing & Telemetry, Redwood Inference
pri yom@redwood.com

Attachments: 2027-11-30_storify_usage_snapshot.csv

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@storify.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@storify.ai, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Charge spike on Nov 30 invoice — request for evidence

Ben/Priyom — thank you for the quick turnaround and for the CSV. The summary aligns with our suspicions — the spikes were tied to a release last night where a client-side retry bug caused mass reconnects for some users.

AP is comfortable releasing payment if Redwood issues a corrective credit for the 28% of the windowed token line and we receive a short technical note we can pass to our engineering team describing the affected pattern. Please also confirm the credit will be reflected as a line adjustment on our next invoice (DEC 2027) and provide a one‑line description we can attach to our ledger.

If Redwood can instead run the deeper de‑duplication correlation and reconcile exact duplicated request_ids within 48 hours, we'd accept that as evidence for a full retroactive removal of duplicated calls — but we understand if that requires additional time.

Can one of you confirm next steps and timeline?

Regards,
Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform, Storify.ai

Attachments: INV-STOR-202711.pdf (original invoice)
